Nigeria startup funding reached US$635 million in the first nine months of 2026, reclaiming Africa’s top position for the first time since 2022.

Nigerian startups raised US$635 million between January and September 2026. That compares with US$247 million in the same period of 2025 — a 157 per cent increase, according to funding data published in October 2026. The result returned Nigeria to the continent’s startup-funding lead.

It is also the highest recorded January-to-September total for Nigeria since 2022. By FurtherAfrica’s reading of the numbers, the rebound reflects a small group of large transactions.

## **Large rounds drive the rebound**
[Moove](https://www.moove.io/) led the charge.

Together, these four deals account for the bulk of Nigeria’s nine-month total.

Top Nigerian startup funding rounds Jan–Sep 2026

|  |  |  |
|-|-|-|
| Moove |  | US$250 million |
| Jumia |  | US$50 million |

Source: October 2026 funding reports

Moove’s round alone represented approximately 68 per cent of Nigeria’s August 2026 funding. That single month generated around US$364 million — illustrating how quickly one large deal can reshape a country’s annual ranking.

web.title: African startup funding crosses $2 billion in 2026
web.description:
African startup funding crosses $2 billion in 2026 - Tech In Africa

Search for:Search

African startups have raised more than **$2 billion in 2026**, excluding exits, reaching the milestone several months earlier than last year.

September is not currently on course to match the strong fundraising totals recorded in June and August, when startups raised **$515 million** and **$455 million** respectively, though a large late-stage deal could still lift the monthly total.

The $2 billion threshold was crossed only a few weeks later than in 2025 and 2023, when it was reached in August.

Based on fundraising patterns in recent years, total funding in 2026 could approach **$3 billion** by year-end.
